top.title: Ireland overcome Fiji to build up head of steam for South Africa clash
top.description: Ireland warmed up for a showdown with world champions South Africa by labouring to a 43-15 Nations Championship victory over Fiji in Dublin. The hosts had won all six previous Test matches between the sides but struggled for fluency and briefly trailed during an uncomfortable opening period at a subdued Aviva Stadium. Robert Baloucoune scored twice in the first half for Andy Farrell’s men after quick-fire tries from Fiji pair Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato overturned Tommy O’Brien’s early opener. Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter, O’Brien and Nick Timoney went over in the second half as Ireland eventually pulled clear to keep alive their hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final. The result leaves Ireland level on 20 points with second-placed England in the northern hemisphere standings – a point below leaders France – ahead of next week’s mouthwatering clash with the Springboks. Head coach Farrell made seven personnel changes and two positional switches to his starting XV following last week’s convincing 42-12 win over Argentina, but insisted the selection was not experimental. Wing O’Brien, one of those recalled, crossed wide on the left to give Ireland an eighth-minute lead. Robert Baloucoune ran in two tries during the first half (Brian Lawless/PA) However, the hosts’ early promise faded after Jamison Gibson-Park had a try ruled out on review due to a knock-on. Fiji centre Tuisova powered over following a line-out maul before Jiuta Wainiqolo burst through a weak Irish defence to tee up captain Yato to put the visitors ahead. Boos rang around the ground when referee Angus Gardner ruled Ireland number eight Timoney had been held up on the line. Baloucoune then crossed twice in quick succession on the right, either side of a disallowed try for Fiji prop Luke Tagi, to restore order. Ronan Kelleher kickstarted Ireland’s second-half scoring (Brian Lawless/PA) But Ireland ended an underwhelming opening period with a slender 17-15 lead as Fiji fly-half Ben Volavola slotted a penalty after home captain Tadhg Beirne was sin-binned. Hooker Kelleher dived over at the start of the second half before O’Brien had to be alert to deny Volavola a breakaway try after he had charged down Sam Prendergast’s attempted clearance. Pop star Niall Horan was among the Lansdowne Road crowd and the scrappy contest gradually started to go in one direction. Nick Timoney wrapped up the victory for Ireland (Brian Lawless/PA) James McNabney’s Ireland debut from the bench lasted a matter of minutes after he was flattened by a swinging arm which resulted in a yellow card for Fiji’s replacement prop Inoke Ravuiwasa. Loosehead prop Porter bulldozed over following that incident before wing O’Brien’s 10th try in as many Tests increased the home side’s advantage further. Timoney completed the scoring by stretching for the line late on, but Ireland have work to do if they are to upset South Africa in seven days’ time.

top.title: From travel troubles to turf shoes, Tulane overcomes unusual obstacles at Rice
top.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 24: Makai Williams #42 of the Tulane Green Wave, Zach Dresch #47 of the Tulane Green Wave and Cayden Dees #58 of the Tulane Green Wave run on the field prior to a game against the UTSA Roadrunners at Yulman Stadium on October 24, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Playing on the road in college football is challenging enough. But for several programs in Week 11 of the 2026 season, getting to the stadium became a battle of its own. On Friday, Nov. 13, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop, disrupting air travel across the country. The stoppage was just the third nationwide ground stop of the 21st century, following the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks and a Jan. 11, 2023 system outage. The Tulane Green Wave were preparing to fly to Houston for their matchup against Rice when their travel plans came to an abrupt halt. With no clear timeline when flights would resume, Tulane pivoted to an alternative that wasn’t a feasible option for many other programs affected by the shutdown. The Green Wave decided to take a nearly six-hour bus ride to Houston. “I want to give a big shoutout to (Chief of Staff) Chris Hatcher and (Director of Football Operations) Rory Thornton,” Tulane head coach Will Hall said. “When we got stopped right there on the tarmac, the efficiency with which they were able to turn this thing around — also credit to our administration, David Harris our athletic director, Patrick Norton, Justin Schemmel, and everybody involved right there to make sure this team was taken care of the best it could.” Tulane’s busses stopped in Lake Charles for a driver change before continuing west on the six-hour trek. The Green Wave ultimately arrived at its Houston hotel past 2 a.m. on Saturday. During the early stages of the trip, Rice and the American Conference agreed to delay the kickoff time two-and-a-half hours, pushing it from 1 p.m. CT to 3:30 p.m. CT. “We ended up bussing over,” Hall said. “We had our normal hotel meetings at the facility. We ate at the facility, we bussed over, we got here about 2:30 in the morning. And thank the league and thank Rice for backing up the kick time a little bit to allow our guys to sleep a little longer. It wasn’t an easy turn of events, but it’s what we want. We know that hard times develop hard men and tough times develop tough men. That’s what we tell our young men, and I thought they handled it elitely. They didn’t in any way use it as an excuse. We knew we had to win this game together. We knew it was gonna take all three phases, and we did it.” Roughly 13 hours after arriving in Houston, Tulane kicked off at First Community Stadium. The Green Wave withstood a sluggish start and turned a 17-6 halftime deficit into a 20-17 victory. A second half shutout from the defense and a late offensive surge allowed the team to secure its second consecutive road win over Hall after a night of complicated travel. “

top.title: '£47m? Why not?' - Former Liverpool centre-back Dejan Lovren tells club to seal bargain permanent deal for Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo
top.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Liverpool defender Dejan Lovren has urged the Reds to trigger their €55 million (£47m) purchase option for Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo. The 27-year-old centre-back has quickly become a mainstay at Anfield since arriving on a season-long deal from the Catalan giants in August. Uruguayan defender impresses on loan Lovren believes Anfield chiefs should waste no time tying down Araujo beyond June 30, 2027 following his seamless transition to English football. Since completing his temporary switch in the summer, the Uruguay international has featured in all 10 of the Merseysiders' opening Premier League matches, starting eight of them. His parent club still hold the defender under contract at Camp Nou until June 2031 . Former centre-back praises physical attributes Having registered 185 appearances and eight goals across all competitions during a six-year spell on Merseyside between 2014 and 2020 before departing for Russian outfit Zenit Saint Petersburg, the Croatian knows what is required at the heart of the backline. Across his English top-flight career, he tallied 162 outings and seven goals - combining 31 games and two strikes at former club Southampton with 131 matches and five goals for the Reds. Speaking to Tribal Football , Lovren explained why the newcomer thrives in England: "I believe the Premier League suits Ronald Araujo more than the Spanish league. Because he is a physically dominant guy, it suits him perfectly. "I believe he will only improve and, I don't know, maybe in the future he can agree to stay permanently. In the Premier League, Liverpool won't be his only option, but Liverpool are smart enough to consider their options, he's quite young at 27. So why not keep him if he's doing so well?" Purchase clause offers bargain value With rival top-flight clubs likely to monitor the centre-half's availability if he returns to Spain next summer, the former Croatia international feels the reported buyout fee represents an opportunity too good for his old employers to ignore. Pressing the hierarchy to make the arrangement permanent, Lovren added: "£47m? Why not? In the near future, he will probably cost £80m, so why not take him at this price and make him an even bigger and better player along the way? He's at a perfect age. He has a good five to six years at the top football level to play. So why not?" Fierce rivals visit Anfield next Addressing his long-term plans recently, Araujo insisted it remains "too early" to decide where he will play his football next season. For now, the defender is focused on helping fourth-placed Liverpool build on their 18-point haul from their opening 10 league outings. Once the international break concludes, the Reds return to top-flight action at Anfield against fierce rivals Manchester United in Matchday 11 on Sunday, November 22.

top.title: 'I still need to improve defensively!' – France surprise package Lucas Da Cunha opens up on Zinedine Zidane's tactical shift
top.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-FRA-TRAINING - AFP France midfielder Lucas Da Cunha has admitted he still needs to improve his defensive work after being deployed in a holding role by Zinedine Zidane. The Como captain discussed his rapid international rise ahead of Les Bleus' crucial UEFA Nations League fixture against Turkey. Lucas Da Cunha embraces surprising France role Como captain Lucas Da Cunha has quickly established himself as a surprise revelation under France coach Zinedine Zidane. Installed in a deep defensive midfield role, the 25-year-old has caught the eye during Les Bleus' UEFA Nations League campaign. Following a narrow defeat to Italy, Zidane's side are gearing up to face Turkey in Bordeaux. Da Cunha is expected to feature heavily as France look to secure qualification. Adapting to a demanding defensive midfield position Traditionally deployed further forward at club level under Cesc Fabregas, Da Cunha admitted that anchoring the French midfield requires a completely different physical and tactical approach . "It's true that I have a different role at Como, where I play further forward. Here, I'm in front of the defense, I don't have to push forward as much as at club level, but I like both positions," Da Cunha explained. "This holding midfield role is new to me; it requires a lot of defensive work, and physically I'm not a monster. I have to win back possession, and I can still improve defensively." Cesc Fabregas and Zinedine Zidane's influence Da Cunha credited his development at club level under Fabregas with preparing him for the tactical demands of international football. Since moving to Italy, the former Rennes youngster has successfully transformed from a winger into a complete central midfielder. The Como skipper also highlighted the personal support he received from Zidane after receiving his maiden senior call-up in September. "He made me feel that I wasn't there for nothing, he talked to me a lot to get to know me, our relationship is very good," Da Cunha revealed. Speaking about captain Kylian Mbappe ahead of the Turkey clash, the midfielder added: "He's in good form and we can feel he's fully committed to us. Like all of us, he's confident before the match." Preparing for high-stakes clash against Turkey France enter Sunday evening's encounter at the Stade Atlantique knowing that victory is essential to bounce back from their San Siro setback and secure quarter-final qualification. While Zidane remains calm following their first defeat in charge, insisting that the squad is entirely focused and not worried, the pressure is on Les Bleus to deliver. With Da Cunha anchoring the midfield and Mbappe leading the attack, France are primed to finish their group stage campaign on a high note.

Just got to play better at the quarterback position.” The defeat is USC’s third of the season, denting its chances for a spot in the 12-team College Football Playoff field. top.title: England are favourites against All Blacks, and fearless Wales are an inspiration
top.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick's side's emphatic 78-15 thrashing of Japan and looks ahead to the match against New Zealand next weekend. I would love to see the England players absolutely bombarded with the favourites tag before their meeting with New Zealand next week. Perhaps even over-egg it a little bit - I want to see how this side handles it. At the end of the day, beating New Zealand or South Africa will likely be a requirement if you want to win a Rugby World Cup. Are England really favourites? Yes, I genuinely believe they are. While victories over Australia and Japan have been encouraging, it was Wales' epic win over the All Blacks on Saturday that has given me real faith that this England side is good enough to compete at the highest level. The key question is whether they can play as they have done over the last two weeks while carrying the favourites tag. England are playing a better style of rugby than New Zealand. I thought the All Blacks' attack, particularly in the second half in Cardiff, was incredibly one-dimensional. That is nothing for England to be afraid of as their own attack has been very slick this campaign. New Zealand aren't going to fix those issues in a week, and England should be capable of soaking up that style of attack defensively. Of course, the All Blacks were missing some frontline players, including Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie, Will Jordan and Jordie Barrett. However, what I saw during the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series was the Springboks beginning to work out that style of play after losing the first Test. They went on to win the next three Tests in a row. Two Tests to turn England into World Cup contenders Having beaten the All Blacks last year, I don't want England to approach this home fixture with an underdog mentality. This side needs to get used to being a contender. The next few weeks could prove crucial in determining whether they are genuine challengers at next year's World Cup. An undefeated autumn, regardless of whether they finish top of the northern hemisphere standings in the Nations Championship, would elevate England to contenders for the Six Nations. Two weeks ago, England would have been delighted to find themselves in this position. Now, the reward could be two massive Tests against the very best. They are not at the level of France or South Africa yet. I think those two sides, particularly after Friday's Test match, are still a little bit ahead of everybody else. However, England have a good chance of facing New Zealand back-to-back over the next two weeks. What an unbelievable opportunity that would be and what a feather in the cap it would represent for this team. It would not only give the players belief in what they are capable of achieving, but also send a message to the rest of the world that they can beat New Zealand and potentially follow that up with another victory over the All Blacks or South Africa. top.title: 3 takeaways from No. 2 Utah’s thrilling victory over No. 23 Arizona
top.description: Arizona wide receiver Isaiah Mizell (17) leaps for a first down against Utah in the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Tucson, Ariz. | Rick Scuteri, Associated Press In a game that saw seven lead changes throughout, the No. 2 Utah Utes overcame a delayed flight, an almost entirely unavailable Wayshawn Parker and a slow start to down Noah Fifita and the No. 23 Arizona Wildcats in an absolute thriller, 40-39 on the road Saturday. The Utes trailed 14-3 before scoring the game’s next 14 points to go up 17-14. From there, the teams went back and forth, exchanging leads as they both showcased their offensive explosiveness led by their respective quarterbacks. Here are three keys that led to Utah’s win. Utah played just well enough to overcome three turnovers A week ago against BYU, the Utes created havoc for rival quarterback Bear Bachmeier as he threw four interceptions, two of which were thrown from inside the 10 when the Cougars were close to scoring. This week it was the other way around. Devon Dampier had a poor pitch that did not find his running back’s hands, and after falling to the ground, found the arms of an Arizona lineman ready to pounce on the first play of the second half, one that Arizona also capitalized on for six points. Dampier also threw an interception in the third quarter that was picked by Arizona’s Jay’Vion Cole at the 1-yard line, where Fifita put together a 99-yard drive to retake the lead. Utah punt returner Mana Carvalho also muffed a punt that gave the ball right back to Arizona. However, the Ute defense held strong for a three-and-out to escape the situation with just giving up a field goal. Ultimately, despite costly mistakes, Dampier’s 204 passing yards and 100 rushing yards were enough to get the job done with assistance from Daniel Bray in the backfield. As the Utes have seen, momentum swings can be the difference in losing and winning. Fortunately for the Utes Saturday, the turnovers did not cost them the game, but head coach Morgan Scalley will surely make ball security a point of emphasis in the week ahead as the Utes look to the TCU Horned Frogs. top.title: Dana White admits he was wrong about Josh Hokit after UFC 334: 'Stock went up with me'
top.description: Josh Hokit may not have won Saturday night at UFC 334, but he still delivered a memorable performance in his first UFC main event . Heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane successfully defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Hokit at New York’s Madison Square Garden, a bout that earned Fight of the Night honors and a $100,000 performance bonus for each man. Although the result marked Hokit's first career defeat in 11 pro fights, UFC CEO Dana White couldn't have been more impressed with the outspoken contender. "It was an incredible fight," White said backstage at the UFC 334 post-fight press conference. "The pace he set was insane, and I think it was freaking everybody out — this smaller guy, the way he was just coming at [Gane]. But even if you look at the significant strikes, they were doubling every round. The total punch stats were massive, too. "If you see the score of the fight, they had it two-to-two going into the last round. I didn't see it that way, but it doesn't tell the story of the fight either. You have to see the fight to believe it." Hokit, 28, has experienced a meteoric rise since joining the promotion a year ago. In that time, White has openly admitted a distaste for how the former NFL player has presented himself with his character work and controversial comments, most notably when Hokit insulted former First Lady Michelle Obama on the White House’s South Lawn . Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit had an all-out war of attrition Saturday at UFC 334. Caleb Bowlin via Getty Images White said he even scored Saturday’s fight four rounds to one in favor of Gane — yet he still believes the fight went perfectly for Hokit, despite a loss being the official result. "What he did was he went in there, and if you really think about going into this fight: How does Josh Hokit win this fight?" White said. "Ciryl Gane moves like a middleweight. He turned it into a street fight from the second the bell rang in the first round. Literally, he didn't win, but he fought the perfect fight. What other way could he possibly fight Ciryl Gane than the way that he did? "My thing was, after the first round, holy s*** — if he can keep this pace for five rounds, Gane's in big trouble. Too big, carries too much muscle and blah, blah, blah. But actually, Gane looked his best in the fourth and fifth rounds. "There's no doubt that Hokit's stock goes up. Even with me," White continued. "I thought this guy was a big-mouth goofball and I hated his schtick and the whole thing. I respect the s*** out of that guy [now]. He is the real deal. Stock went up with me." Hokit beat two longtime heavyweight contenders, Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis , to earn his title shot. The latter came on the big stage that was UFC Freedom 250 at the White House in June. top.title: 'Of course it is annoying!' – Zinedine Zidane blasts media reports over his relationship with Kylian Mbappe
top.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-FRA-TRAINING - AFP France head coach Zinedine Zidane has strongly denied any friction between himself and captain Kylian Mbappe. Speaking ahead of their crucial UEFA Nations League fixture against Turkey, Zidane branded media speculation regarding their relationship as entirely false and annoying. Zidane hits back at Mbappe rift rumours France head coach Zinedine Zidane has firmly put to bed any talk of a strained relationship with national team captain Kylian Mbappe. Speaking ahead of Sunday's crucial UEFA Nations League clash against Turkey in Bordeaux, Zidane addressed media speculation head-on . With Les Bleus needing a victory to secure qualification on a high note, the manager stressed that unity within the camp remains absolute. 'The relationship is perfectly fine' Press conference inquiries quickly turned to rumoured friction between the manager and his star striker ahead of the Stade Atlantique fixture. With an impassive expression, Zidane made it clear that stories of a fallout are completely wide of the mark. "I don't quite understand what's being written," Zidane stated firmly. "I'm not going to get into the debate; the relationship is perfect. For the player as well as for me. I can't stop what's being said." When pressed on whether the ongoing reports had frustrated him, the former midfielder admitted that the speculation is wearing thin. "Yes, the things that come back to me, of course, are quite annoying," he added. Tactical plans and squad updates for Turkey On the pitch, Zidane confirmed that Mbappe will start in his preferred position, leading a 4-3-3 attacking trident as France look to bounce back from a 3-1 defeat against Italy. "Of course it changes everything, we'd rather have him with us than not have him," Zidane noted regarding his talisman. Elsewhere in camp, young forward Désiré Doué trained despite struggling with an unstable tooth following an elbow from Davide Frattesi. Meanwhile, players like Michael Olise and Bradley Barcola are tipped to support Mbappe in attack, with defensive changes expected as Les Bleus chase victory. All eyes on Bordeaux showdown with Turkey Sunday evening's encounter at the Stade Atlantique carries massive significance as Les Bleus aim to bounce back and seal their qualification status in style. Zidane's men know that a strong performance against the Turks will banish memories of their San Siro setback. With the squad fully focused and their captain primed to lead the line, France are ready to deliver a statement display in their final group outing.

top.title: “Tennessee Broke This Man’s Soul”: Fans React to Mike Elko “Begging for His Job” With His “Utter Apology” After Texas A&M’s Loss
top.description: Texas A&M Aggies head coach Mike Elko during warm ups before Auburn Tigers take on Texas A&M Aggies at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Ala., on Saturday, Nov. 23, 2024. Mike Elko has not been a name that many will hear about this season, but he made himself known on Saturday – for the wrong reasons. Shortly after Texas A&M suffered a 7-22 home drubbing against Tennessee, the Aggies’ head coach opened his post-game presser with this statement: “Utter apology with everything that I have to everybody that supports this program. Thank you for turning out; you deserve so much better. Give me a chance & we will get this fixed and put a much better product on the field.” His attempt at contrition, unfortunately, was met with derision and condemnation from fans: The game was notable for some underwhelming quarterback performances. For Texas A&M, Marcel Reed completed only nine of 22 attempts for 71 yards and was intercepted once, while Brady Hart added another pick. The team’s only touchdown came on a KJ Edwards run. George MacIntyre, meanwhile, had just 109 yards for Tennessee before exiting in the third quarter with a knee injury, but he set up two field goals for Cooper Ranvier. After taking over, Faizon Brandon threw a touchdown pass to DeSaahn Brame and then set up three more field goals. Texas A&M HC Mike Elko discusses Aggies’ offensive woes vs. Tennessee All told, Mike Elko had just one word to describe how Texas A&M’s offense fared on Saturday: “Pathetic.” He continued: “The wind played a big role,” explained Elko. “The (pass) rush played a bigger role. Our inability to give (Marcel Reed) any time to see anything — they’re very multiple on defense — so the pressure created a massive challenge trying to do anything.” The Aggies will visit Oklahoma next week. Kickoff is at 11 a.m. CT. top.title: Coco Gauff’s Ex-Coach Urges Aryna Sabalenka to Make Major Changes To Her Team After WTA Finals Heartbreak: “Hard Questions to Figure Out”
top.description: Aug 8, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, Canada; Aryna Sabalenka reacts after missing a point against Ekaterina Alexandrova (not pictured) during the fourth round at the National Bank Open at Sobeys Stadium. © John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Coco Gauff’s former coach Brad Gilbert weighed in on Aryna Sabalenka’s WTA Finals disappointment, urging the Belarusian to make changes to her coaching team. The Belarusian stopped working with Max Mirnyi ahead of the WTA Finals, but is still working with head coach Anton Dubrov and performance coach Jason Stacy. Sabalenka’s run at the WTA Finals ended after she lost two of her three round-robin matches. She failed to win a Grand Slam this season and did not lift a title since the Sunshine Double. Sabalenka was also surpassed by Elena Rybakina for the top spot in the world rankings. Noting Sabalenka’s lackluster run, Gilbert suggested she make changes to her team. He opined that if he were in Sabalenka’s place, he would have promoted Mirnyi as head coach. On the Big T podcast , Gilbert also suggested that she make changes to her serve and forehand. “I think the biggest thing for this off-season is going to be the serve, and I do feel all of a sudden the forehand, which I do think is her best shot, has been letting her down a lot. I think she might need some changes to her team. I heard she let Max Mirnyi go. I would have promoted him to head coach. She’s got some hard questions to figure out this off-season to start the year very positively because she’s played well Down Under (at the Australian Open) the last few years.” Sabalenka has won the Australian Open twice, in 2023 and 2024. Aryna Sabalenka apologizes after video of her comments to fans spreads online Aryna Sabalenka issued an apology after a video of her comments to fans surfaced online after her WTA Finals loss to Elina Svitolina. “I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online. My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment. That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.” Screenshot of Aryna Sabalenka’s Instagram story. Elina Svitolina, meanwhile, advanced to the final of the year-end event, where she will take on Mirra Andreeva. top.title: 2027: Inuwa Yahaya flags off APC campaign, targets 1m votes for Tinubu
top.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe BAJOGA, the headquarters of Funakaye Local Government Area of Gombe State, was the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign flag-off on Saturday, as Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya declared the state ready to support President Bola Tinubu and other candidates of the ruling party in the 2027 general elections. At the rally, which attracted party supporters and political stakeholders from across the state, Inuwa Yahaya said the APC was targeting at least one million votes for Tinubu, expressing confidence that the party would win all elective positions in Gombe. The event was attended by the Special Adviser to the President on Political and Other Matters, Hon. Ibrahim Kabir Masari; APC Deputy National Chairman (North), Hon. Ali Bukar Dalori; former governors, members of the National Assembly and other party chieftains. top.title: Manchester City Eyeing £35 Million-Rated Lens Goalkeeper Amid Gianluigi Donnarumma Struggles
top.description: Manchester City Eyeing £35 Million-Rated Lens Goalkeeper Amid Gianluigi Donnarumma Struggles Gianluigi Donnarumma has struggled in net for Manchester City of late. More Videos Gianluigi Donnarumma remains Enzo Maresca’s first-choice goalkeeper, but it has not been the most convincing start to the season for the Italian. A number of costly errors have placed his form under scrutiny, forcing Maresca to publicly back his No. 1 on more than one occasion and prompting some supporters to argue that their side needs more competition between the sticks. With Geronimo Rulli approaching 35 years of age, that competition would likely have to come from the transfer market - which is where a new name linked with Manchester City will raise eyebrows. It’s safe to assume that the club’s recruitment staff have continued to track the next generation of goalkeepers across Europe even after the signing of Donnarumma, and fresh rumours suggest the search has taken them to France. Trophy-winning Lens shotstopper being considered by Man City The name in question is RC Lens goalkeeper Robin Risser, who was part of France’s World Cup squad in the summer after a meteoric rise in senior football. According to Swiss outlet 4-4-2.ch , as relayed by Sports Mole , Manchester City are leading the chase for the 21-year-old and are considering an opening bid of around £26 million ahead of the summer window. Lens, however, are holding out for at least £35 million for a player contracted until June 2030. Risser was central to a superb 2025-26 campaign at Lens as they finished second in Ligue 1 and lifted the Coupe de France. That form earned him the UNFP Goalkeeper of the Year award and a place in the competition’s Team of the Year. The 6ft 4in Risser boasts a commanding aerial presence and composure on the ball, making him exactly the kind of profile that would suit Manchester City ’s build-up play. The sticking point is a sell-on clause inserted by Strasbourg, reported as 25 per cent of the total fee - or 25 per cent of the profit according to L’Équipe - meaning a significant chunk of any sale would be owed to his old club. Risser’s current season has admittedly been more difficult than the last, not least with a chastening 9-1 UEFA Champions League defeat at home to Como earlier this month. His standing at international level has held firm, though, with the youngster called up under both Didier Deschamps and new France boss Zinedine Zidane. That promise has not gone unnoticed elsewhere. Liverpool and Manchester United are reportedly both keeping tabs, as are Serie A pair Inter Milan and Juventus, while Newcastle United and Tottenham have shown interest in the past. No formal offers have been tabled as yet.

top.title: Dominik Livakovic talks life in Barcelona, training and game-time under Flick
top.description: Dominik Livakovic talks life in Barcelona, training and game-time under Flick Dominik Livakovic was somewhat of a surprise signing for Barcelona when the club roped him in the summer for a fee of just €2 million. It was an investment made keeping in mind Wojciech Szczesny’s future, with Livakovic immediately being promoted as the main alternative to Joan Garcia. Currently on duty with the Croatian national team, Livakovic has opened up about his time at Barcelona so far, including his lack of game-time among other things. Livakovic on game-time at Barcelona Livakovic has won 84 caps for Croatia. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Livakovic was asked whether or not his lack of minutes at Barcelona affects his standing in the Croatian national team. “I play for Barcelona. I’m just a young man from Zadar, and I’m very proud of that. I’ve already kept goal for this great club. I train and wait for my chance, and I feel like I’m in good shape,” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). Livakovic, who started in the recent game against England , went on to describe the training process at Barcelona, which he labelled tough. The goalkeeper added that he is waiting for his chance to impress. “Training at Barcelona really is very tough, because we’re talking about the best players in the world. It would be ideal to play in goal in every match, but I’m waiting patiently for my chance ,” he added. Livakovic has so far made only one appearance for Barcelona since joining the club in the summer. That lone appearance came against Sevilla earlier in the campaign. Livakovic on being awarded Fiery Heart trophy Livakovic is regarded highly in Croatian football. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Meanwhile, it was a special day for Livakovic as he was awarded the Fiery Heart trophy for his selfless service to the Croatian national team. After stepping away from coaching in 2016, Ryan joined ESPN as an NFL analyst, primarily appearing on “Sunday NFL Countdown.” However, he turned himself in to Nashville authorities early Wednesday morning after allegedly running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck on Broadway Street. Ryan drove away but eventually stopped at a red light, where he got out and argued with the pedestrians. He then returned to his vehicle and left the scene. Authorities later identified his license plate and traced the truck’s registration to him. The former NFL coach now faces six misdemeanor counts: leaving the scene of an accident (2), failure to give information or render aid (2), and failure to obey a traffic control signal (2). nigeria.title: Meet 2 African countries to ever break into top five FIFA World Ranking
nigeria.description: Only two African countries have ever reached the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking, with Nigeria and Morocco achieving the historic feat more than three decades apart. The Super Eagles of Nigeria were the first African team to break into the world’s top five, reaching fifth place in April 1994. The achievement came during one of the most memorable periods in Nigerian football history, following the country’s victory at the 1994 Africa Cup of Nations in Tunisia. Nigeria, coached by Clemens Westerhof, had a talented generation featuring Rashidi Yekini, Daniel Amokachi, Emmanuel Amunike, Finidi George, Sunday Oliseh and Austin Jay-Jay Okocha. The Super Eagles also made their debut at the 1994 FIFA World Cup in the United States, where they topped their group before being eliminated by Italy in the round of 16. For 32 years, Nigeria’s fifth-place ranking remained the highest position ever achieved by an African national team. However, Morocco joined the exclusive list in September 2026 after climbing to fifth in the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. The Atlas Lions’ rise followed a period of impressive performances, including their historic run to the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Morocco had also made history at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, becoming the first African country to reach the semi-finals of the competition. Their latest achievement saw them equal Nigeria’s record, making them the second African country to reach fifth place in the global ranking. According to FIFA, Morocco’s achievement matched the highest position ever attained by an African national team, a record Nigeria had held since April 1994. The two African countries are: Nigeria: Fifth place in April 1994. Morocco: Fifth place in September 2026. The two countries have therefore written their names into African football history, becoming the only representatives of the continent to reach the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. nigeria.description: …404 ‘arrested’ in 20 months By Nnamdi Ojiego The image of an elderly grandmother or grandfather being led away by anti-narcotics officers over alleged involvement in drug trafficking is one that challenges conventional perceptions of who participates in the illicit drug trade. Yet, a succession of arrests involving people in their 60s, 70s and even older has brought an uncomfortable question to the fore: Why are people who should ordinarily be enjoying their retirement years becoming involved in the dangerous business of transporting, storing and distributing illicit drugs? In Nigeria, the figures supplied by Femi Babafemi, spokesperson of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) suggest that the phenomenon deserves closer attention. The agency arrested 240 persons aged 60 and above for drug-related offences in 2025, comprising 191 men and 49 women. Between January and August 2026, another 164 elderly suspects, including 128 men and 36 women, were arrested. The figures bring the total number of elderly persons arrested within the 20-month period to 404. Men accounted for the overwhelming majority, representing approximately 80 per cent of the arrests in 2025 and 78 per cent in the first eight months of 2026. Calculated strategy Although the 2026 figures cover only eight months and cannot be directly compared with the full-year 2025 total, the number of arrests already recorded points to the continued involvement of older people in drug-related activities. It also raises questions about the circumstances drawing them into a trade whose consequences include lengthy imprisonment, financial ruin, damaged family relationships and, in some cases, serious health risks. The NDLEA also reported seizing 6,998.77 kilogrammes of illicit drugs in connection with elderly suspects in 2025, compared with 1,479.988 kilogrammes between January and August 2026. From couriers to local dealers The cases recorded by the NDLEA in 2026 provide a glimpse into the different ways older people are becoming involved in the illicit drug trade. The concerns have been heightened by fresh incidents of political violence in different parts of the country, including Calabar, Cross River State, Asaba, Delta State, and Sokoto, where political supporters and opposition figures have reportedly come under attack. The North-East accounted for the highest number of fatalities, with 409 deaths. The report also documented 16 election-related incidents in October, compared with 14 in September, representing a 14.29 per cent increase. Attacks on campaign gatherings and convoys accounted for 11 of the 16 incidents. The incidents affected several political parties, including the All Progressives Congress (APC) and African Democratic Congress (ADC), which each recorded four cases, while the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) recorded three. Two of the incidents were fatal. Ifeanyi Nwolie died from gunshot injuries sustained during the NDC campaign launch in Enugu on October 10. In Ebonyi, gunmen attacked the convoy of NDC candidate, Rollins Offia-Nwali, on October 22, killing one person, injuring three others and burning his vehicle. The candidate reportedly escaped. business.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down. entertainment.title: Mark Your Calendars! Lagos International Theatre Festival Returns to MUSON Centre This November
entertainment.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. The stage is everywhere.” Festival Director, Vanessa Jev , said the diversity of voices at this year’s festival was particularly exciting, with Nigerian artists joining performers from Kenya, Canada and Brazil to create opportunities for audiences to experience different cultures and perspectives. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. entertainment.title: “Lagos Gave Me My Greatest Successes and Deepest Heartbreak”: DJ Cuppy Opens Up in Ifeoluwa Documentary
entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it. sports.title: Ireland overcome Fiji to build up head of steam for South Africa clash
sports.description: Ireland warmed up for a showdown with world champions South Africa by labouring to a 43-15 Nations Championship victory over Fiji in Dublin. The hosts had won all six previous Test matches between the sides but struggled for fluency and briefly trailed during an uncomfortable opening period at a subdued Aviva Stadium. Robert Baloucoune scored twice in the first half for Andy Farrell’s men after quick-fire tries from Fiji pair Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato overturned Tommy O’Brien’s early opener. Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter, O’Brien and Nick Timoney went over in the second half as Ireland eventually pulled clear to keep alive their hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final. The result leaves Ireland level on 20 points with second-placed England in the northern hemisphere standings – a point below leaders France – ahead of next week’s mouthwatering clash with the Springboks. Head coach Farrell made seven personnel changes and two positional switches to his starting XV following last week’s convincing 42-12 win over Argentina, but insisted the selection was not experimental. Wing O’Brien, one of those recalled, crossed wide on the left to give Ireland an eighth-minute lead. Robert Baloucoune ran in two tries during the first half (Brian Lawless/PA) However, the hosts’ early promise faded after Jamison Gibson-Park had a try ruled out on review due to a knock-on. Fiji centre Tuisova powered over following a line-out maul before Jiuta Wainiqolo burst through a weak Irish defence to tee up captain Yato to put the visitors ahead. Boos rang around the ground when referee Angus Gardner ruled Ireland number eight Timoney had been held up on the line. Baloucoune then crossed twice in quick succession on the right, either side of a disallowed try for Fiji prop Luke Tagi, to restore order. Ronan Kelleher kickstarted Ireland’s second-half scoring (Brian Lawless/PA) But Ireland ended an underwhelming opening period with a slender 17-15 lead as Fiji fly-half Ben Volavola slotted a penalty after home captain Tadhg Beirne was sin-binned. Hooker Kelleher dived over at the start of the second half before O’Brien had to be alert to deny Volavola a breakaway try after he had charged down Sam Prendergast’s attempted clearance. Pop star Niall Horan was among the Lansdowne Road crowd and the scrappy contest gradually started to go in one direction. Nick Timoney wrapped up the victory for Ireland (Brian Lawless/PA) James McNabney’s Ireland debut from the bench lasted a matter of minutes after he was flattened by a swinging arm which resulted in a yellow card for Fiji’s replacement prop Inoke Ravuiwasa. Loosehead prop Porter bulldozed over following that incident before wing O’Brien’s 10th try in as many Tests increased the home side’s advantage further. Timoney completed the scoring by stretching for the line late on, but Ireland have work to do if they are to upset South Africa in seven days’ time.

sports.title: From travel troubles to turf shoes, Tulane overcomes unusual obstacles at Rice
sports.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 24: Makai Williams #42 of the Tulane Green Wave, Zach Dresch #47 of the Tulane Green Wave and Cayden Dees #58 of the Tulane Green Wave run on the field prior to a game against the UTSA Roadrunners at Yulman Stadium on October 24, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Playing on the road in college football is challenging enough. But for several programs in Week 11 of the 2026 season, getting to the stadium became a battle of its own. On Friday, Nov. 13, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop, disrupting air travel across the country. The stoppage was just the third nationwide ground stop of the 21st century, following the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks and a Jan. 11, 2023 system outage. The Tulane Green Wave were preparing to fly to Houston for their matchup against Rice when their travel plans came to an abrupt halt. With no clear timeline when flights would resume, Tulane pivoted to an alternative that wasn’t a feasible option for many other programs affected by the shutdown. The Green Wave decided to take a nearly six-hour bus ride to Houston. “I want to give a big shoutout to (Chief of Staff) Chris Hatcher and (Director of Football Operations) Rory Thornton,” Tulane head coach Will Hall said. “When we got stopped right there on the tarmac, the efficiency with which they were able to turn this thing around — also credit to our administration, David Harris our athletic director, Patrick Norton, Justin Schemmel, and everybody involved right there to make sure this team was taken care of the best it could.” Tulane’s busses stopped in Lake Charles for a driver change before continuing west on the six-hour trek. The Green Wave ultimately arrived at its Houston hotel past 2 a.m. on Saturday. During the early stages of the trip, Rice and the American Conference agreed to delay the kickoff time two-and-a-half hours, pushing it from 1 p.m. CT to 3:30 p.m. CT. “We ended up bussing over,” Hall said. “We had our normal hotel meetings at the facility. We ate at the facility, we bussed over, we got here about 2:30 in the morning. And thank the league and thank Rice for backing up the kick time a little bit to allow our guys to sleep a little longer. It wasn’t an easy turn of events, but it’s what we want. We know that hard times develop hard men and tough times develop tough men. That’s what we tell our young men, and I thought they handled it elitely. They didn’t in any way use it as an excuse. We knew we had to win this game together. We knew it was gonna take all three phases, and we did it.” Roughly 13 hours after arriving in Houston, Tulane kicked off at First Community Stadium. The Green Wave withstood a sluggish start and turned a 17-6 halftime deficit into a 20-17 victory. sports.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Liverpool defender Dejan Lovren has urged the Reds to trigger their €55 million (£47m) purchase option for Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo. The 27-year-old centre-back has quickly become a mainstay at Anfield since arriving on a season-long deal from the Catalan giants in August. Uruguayan defender impresses on loan Lovren believes Anfield chiefs should waste no time tying down Araujo beyond June 30, 2027 following his seamless transition to English football. Since completing his temporary switch in the summer, the Uruguay international has featured in all 10 of the Merseysiders' opening Premier League matches, starting eight of them. His parent club still hold the defender under contract at Camp Nou until June 2031 . Former centre-back praises physical attributes Having registered 185 appearances and eight goals across all competitions during a six-year spell on Merseyside between 2014 and 2020 before departing for Russian outfit Zenit Saint Petersburg, the Croatian knows what is required at the heart of the backline. Across his English top-flight career, he tallied 162 outings and seven goals - combining 31 games and two strikes at former club Southampton with 131 matches and five goals for the Reds. Speaking to Tribal Football , Lovren explained why the newcomer thrives in England: "I believe the Premier League suits Ronald Araujo more than the Spanish league. Because he is a physically dominant guy, it suits him perfectly. "I believe he will only improve and, I don't know, maybe in the future he can agree to stay permanently. In the Premier League, Liverpool won't be his only option, but Liverpool are smart enough to consider their options, he's quite young at 27. So why not keep him if he's doing so well?" Purchase clause offers bargain value With rival top-flight clubs likely to monitor the centre-half's availability if he returns to Spain next summer, the former Croatia international feels the reported buyout fee represents an opportunity too good for his old employers to ignore. Pressing the hierarchy to make the arrangement permanent, Lovren added: "£47m? Why not? In the near future, he will probably cost £80m, so why not take him at this price and make him an even bigger and better player along the way? He's at a perfect age. He has a good five to six years at the top football level to play. So why not?" Fierce rivals visit Anfield next Addressing his long-term plans recently, Araujo insisted it remains "too early" to decide where he will play his football next season. For now, the defender is focused on helping fourth-placed Liverpool build on their 18-point haul from their opening 10 league outings. Once the international break concludes, the Reds return to top-flight action at Anfield against fierce rivals Manchester United in Matchday 11 on Sunday, November 22.

The Como captain discussed his rapid international rise ahead of Les Bleus' crucial UEFA Nations League fixture against Turkey. Lucas Da Cunha embraces surprising France role Como captain Lucas Da Cunha has quickly established himself as a surprise revelation under France coach Zinedine Zidane. Installed in a deep defensive midfield role, the 25-year-old has caught the eye during Les Bleus' UEFA Nations League campaign. Following a narrow defeat to Italy, Zidane's side are gearing up to face Turkey in Bordeaux. Da Cunha is expected to feature heavily as France look to secure qualification. Adapting to a demanding defensive midfield position Traditionally deployed further forward at club level under Cesc Fabregas, Da Cunha admitted that anchoring the French midfield requires a completely different physical and tactical approach . "It's true that I have a different role at Como, where I play further forward. Here, I'm in front of the defense, I don't have to push forward as much as at club level, but I like both positions," Da Cunha explained. "This holding midfield role is new to me; it requires a lot of defensive work, and physically I'm not a monster. I have to win back possession, and I can still improve defensively." Cesc Fabregas and Zinedine Zidane's influence Da Cunha credited his development at club level under Fabregas with preparing him for the tactical demands of international football. Since moving to Italy, the former Rennes youngster has successfully transformed from a winger into a complete central midfielder. The Como skipper also highlighted the personal support he received from Zidane after receiving his maiden senior call-up in September. "He made me feel that I wasn't there for nothing, he talked to me a lot to get to know me, our relationship is very good," Da Cunha revealed. sports.title: England are favourites against All Blacks, and fearless Wales are an inspiration
sports.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick's side's emphatic 78-15 thrashing of Japan and looks ahead to the match against New Zealand next weekend. I would love to see the England players absolutely bombarded with the favourites tag before their meeting with New Zealand next week. Perhaps even over-egg it a little bit - I want to see how this side handles it. At the end of the day, beating New Zealand or South Africa will likely be a requirement if you want to win a Rugby World Cup. Are England really favourites? Yes, I genuinely believe they are. While victories over Australia and Japan have been encouraging, it was Wales' epic win over the All Blacks on Saturday that has given me real faith that this England side is good enough to compete at the highest level. The key question is whether they can play as they have done over the last two weeks while carrying the favourites tag. England are playing a better style of rugby than New Zealand. I thought the All Blacks' attack, particularly in the second half in Cardiff, was incredibly one-dimensional. That is nothing for England to be afraid of as their own attack has been very slick this campaign. New Zealand aren't going to fix those issues in a week, and England should be capable of soaking up that style of attack defensively. Of course, the All Blacks were missing some frontline players, including Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie, Will Jordan and Jordie Barrett. However, what I saw during the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series was the Springboks beginning to work out that style of play after losing the first Test. They went on to win the next three Tests in a row. Two Tests to turn England into World Cup contenders Having beaten the All Blacks last year, I don't want England to approach this home fixture with an underdog mentality. This side needs to get used to being a contender. The next few weeks could prove crucial in determining whether they are genuine challengers at next year's World Cup. An undefeated autumn, regardless of whether they finish top of the northern hemisphere standings in the Nations Championship, would elevate England to contenders for the Six Nations. Two weeks ago, England would have been delighted to find themselves in this position. Now, the reward could be two massive Tests against the very best. They are not at the level of France or South Africa yet. I think those two sides, particularly after Friday's Test match, are still a little bit ahead of everybody else. However, England have a good chance of facing New Zealand back-to-back over the next two weeks. What an unbelievable opportunity that would be and what a feather in the cap it would represent for this team. It would not only give the players belief in what they are capable of achieving, but also send a message to the rest of the world that they can beat New Zealand and potentially follow that up with another victory over the All Blacks or South Africa. sports.title: 3 takeaways from No. 2 Utah’s thrilling victory over No. 23 Arizona
sports.description: Arizona wide receiver Isaiah Mizell (17) leaps for a first down against Utah in the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Tucson, Ariz. | Rick Scuteri, Associated Press In a game that saw seven lead changes throughout, the No. 2 Utah Utes overcame a delayed flight, an almost entirely unavailable Wayshawn Parker and a slow start to down Noah Fifita and the No. 23 Arizona Wildcats in an absolute thriller, 40-39 on the road Saturday. The Utes trailed 14-3 before scoring the game’s next 14 points to go up 17-14. From there, the teams went back and forth, exchanging leads as they both showcased their offensive explosiveness led by their respective quarterbacks. Here are three keys that led to Utah’s win. Utah played just well enough to overcome three turnovers A week ago against BYU, the Utes created havoc for rival quarterback Bear Bachmeier as he threw four interceptions, two of which were thrown from inside the 10 when the Cougars were close to scoring. This week it was the other way around. Devon Dampier had a poor pitch that did not find his running back’s hands, and after falling to the ground, found the arms of an Arizona lineman ready to pounce on the first play of the second half, one that Arizona also capitalized on for six points. Dampier also threw an interception in the third quarter that was picked by Arizona’s Jay’Vion Cole at the 1-yard line, where Fifita put together a 99-yard drive to retake the lead. Utah punt returner Mana Carvalho also muffed a punt that gave the ball right back to Arizona. However, the Ute defense held strong for a three-and-out to escape the situation with just giving up a field goal. Ultimately, despite costly mistakes, Dampier’s 204 passing yards and 100 rushing yards were enough to get the job done with assistance from Daniel Bray in the backfield. As the Utes have seen, momentum swings can be the difference in losing and winning. sports.description: Josh Hokit may not have won Saturday night at UFC 334, but he still delivered a memorable performance in his first UFC main event . Heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane successfully defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Hokit at New York’s Madison Square Garden, a bout that earned Fight of the Night honors and a $100,000 performance bonus for each man. Although the result marked Hokit's first career defeat in 11 pro fights, UFC CEO Dana White couldn't have been more impressed with the outspoken contender. "It was an incredible fight," White said backstage at the UFC 334 post-fight press conference. "The pace he set was insane, and I think it was freaking everybody out — this smaller guy, the way he was just coming at [Gane]. But even if you look at the significant strikes, they were doubling every round. The total punch stats were massive, too. "If you see the score of the fight, they had it two-to-two going into the last round. I didn't see it that way, but it doesn't tell the story of the fight either. You have to see the fight to believe it." Hokit, 28, has experienced a meteoric rise since joining the promotion a year ago. In that time, White has openly admitted a distaste for how the former NFL player has presented himself with his character work and controversial comments, most notably when Hokit insulted former First Lady Michelle Obama on the White House’s South Lawn . Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit had an all-out war of attrition Saturday at UFC 334. Caleb Bowlin via Getty Images White said he even scored Saturday’s fight four rounds to one in favor of Gane — yet he still believes the fight went perfectly for Hokit, despite a loss being the official result. sports.title: Manchester City Eyeing £35 Million-Rated Lens Goalkeeper Amid Gianluigi Donnarumma Struggles
sports.description: Manchester City Eyeing £35 Million-Rated Lens Goalkeeper Amid Gianluigi Donnarumma Struggles Gianluigi Donnarumma has struggled in net for Manchester City of late. More Videos Gianluigi Donnarumma remains Enzo Maresca’s first-choice goalkeeper, but it has not been the most convincing start to the season for the Italian. A number of costly errors have placed his form under scrutiny, forcing Maresca to publicly back his No. 1 on more than one occasion and prompting some supporters to argue that their side needs more competition between the sticks. With Geronimo Rulli approaching 35 years of age, that competition would likely have to come from the transfer market - which is where a new name linked with Manchester City will raise eyebrows. It’s safe to assume that the club’s recruitment staff have continued to track the next generation of goalkeepers across Europe even after the signing of Donnarumma, and fresh rumours suggest the search has taken them to France. Trophy-winning Lens shotstopper being considered by Man City The name in question is RC Lens goalkeeper Robin Risser, who was part of France’s World Cup squad in the summer after a meteoric rise in senior football. According to Swiss outlet 4-4-2.ch , as relayed by Sports Mole , Manchester City are leading the chase for the 21-year-old and are considering an opening bid of around £26 million ahead of the summer window. Lens, however, are holding out for at least £35 million for a player contracted until June 2030. Risser was central to a superb 2025-26 campaign at Lens as they finished second in Ligue 1 and lifted the Coupe de France. That form earned him the UNFP Goalkeeper of the Year award and a place in the competition’s Team of the Year. The 6ft 4in Risser boasts a commanding aerial presence and composure on the ball, making him exactly the kind of profile that would suit Manchester City ’s build-up play. The sticking point is a sell-on clause inserted by Strasbourg, reported as 25 per cent of the total fee - or 25 per cent of the profit according to L’Équipe - meaning a significant chunk of any sale would be owed to his old club. Risser’s current season has admittedly been more difficult than the last, not least with a chastening 9-1 UEFA Champions League defeat at home to Como earlier this month. His standing at international level has held firm, though, with the youngster called up under both Didier Deschamps and new France boss Zinedine Zidane. That promise has not gone unnoticed elsewhere. Liverpool and Manchester United are reportedly both keeping tabs, as are Serie A pair Inter Milan and Juventus, while Newcastle United and Tottenham have shown interest in the past. No formal offers have been tabled as yet.

sports.title: Dominik Livakovic talks life in Barcelona, training and game-time under Flick
sports.description: Dominik Livakovic talks life in Barcelona, training and game-time under Flick Dominik Livakovic was somewhat of a surprise signing for Barcelona when the club roped him in the summer for a fee of just €2 million. It was an investment made keeping in mind Wojciech Szczesny’s future, with Livakovic immediately being promoted as the main alternative to Joan Garcia. Currently on duty with the Croatian national team, Livakovic has opened up about his time at Barcelona so far, including his lack of game-time among other things. Livakovic on game-time at Barcelona Livakovic has won 84 caps for Croatia. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Livakovic was asked whether or not his lack of minutes at Barcelona affects his standing in the Croatian national team. “I play for Barcelona. I’m just a young man from Zadar, and I’m very proud of that. I’ve already kept goal for this great club. I train and wait for my chance, and I feel like I’m in good shape,” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). Livakovic, who started in the recent game against England , went on to describe the training process at Barcelona, which he labelled tough. The goalkeeper added that he is waiting for his chance to impress. “Training at Barcelona really is very tough, because we’re talking about the best players in the world. It would be ideal to play in goal in every match, but I’m waiting patiently for my chance ,” he added. Livakovic has so far made only one appearance for Barcelona since joining the club in the summer. That lone appearance came against Sevilla earlier in the campaign. Livakovic on being awarded Fiery Heart trophy Livakovic is regarded highly in Croatian football. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Meanwhile, it was a special day for Livakovic as he was awarded the Fiery Heart trophy for his selfless service to the Croatian national team. Speaking about the accolade, the goalkeeper said, “This award has made me very happy, because it comes from the fans who give football its passion and special emotions. “ “I truly care, from the bottom of my heart, about the national team’s success, and I’m happy that the fans recognized that and appreciated it in this way. “ Livakovic added that it’s an honour to follow in the footsteps of Croatian legends such as Ivan Perisic and Luka Modric, previous recipients of the award. “It’s wonderful to follow in the footsteps of Luka and Perišić, who won this award before me, and that alone shows its value. “I thank everyone who took part in the voting, and I extend a special thank-you to all the fans who continue to support us, whether things are going well or we’re going through tougher times,” he concluded.

sports.title: ‘A Lot Of Negative Things Happened’ — Super Bowl-Winning HC Pushes Mike Vrabel’s Patriots To Clean Up Their Act
sports.description: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. The New England Patriots have shown they can move the ball and put points on the board, but their recent performances have exposed a problem that keeps putting them in difficult positions. Falling behind early has forced Mike Vrabel’s team to spend too much time chasing games instead of controlling them. Super Bowl-winning coach Jon Gruden believes the Patriots need to address that habit before it costs them again. Jon Gruden Urges Mike Vrabel’s Patriots to Fix Their Slow Starts Gruden shared his assessment in a video on X, pointing out that New England’s overall offensive production has not been the problem. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach, who led the team to a Super Bowl XXXVII victory, believes the Patriots must translate that production into better openings. “The Patriots’ offense averages 23.4 points per game. That’s 14th in the league. They’re eighth in total offense. It’s a credit to them,” Gruden said. “They average 369 yards a game, rank 10th in rushing and ninth in passing. But they have to resolve the slow starts. There’s nothing worse than a slow start.” He then highlighted how New England has fallen behind in recent games. Against Green Bay in Week 9, the Patriots allowed a 17-0 lead after a difficult opening stretch. sports.title: Rex Ryan’s Status for ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’ Revealed After Arrest
sports.description: BEVERLY HILLS, CA - JULY 26: Former NFL coach & ESPN analyst Rex Ryan of 'ESPN's Sunday's NFL Countdown' speaks onstage during the ESPN portion of the 2017 Summer Television Critics Association Press Tour at The Beverly Hilton Hotel on July 26, 2017 in Beverly Hills, California. (Photo by Frederick M. Brown/Getty Images) Getty Former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills head coach Rex Ryan was in the news for the wrong reasons this week. After stepping away from coaching in 2016, Ryan joined ESPN as an NFL analyst, primarily appearing on “Sunday NFL Countdown.” However, he turned himself in to Nashville authorities early Wednesday morning after allegedly running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck on Broadway Street. Ryan drove away but eventually stopped at a red light, where he got out and argued with the pedestrians. He then returned to his vehicle and left the scene. Authorities later identified his license plate and traced the truck’s registration to him. The former NFL coach now faces six misdemeanor counts: leaving the scene of an accident (2), failure to give information or render aid (2), and failure to obey a traffic control signal (2). Will Ryan Be on ESPN Sunday Morning? With Sunday morning approaching, a big question is whether Ryan will appear alongside the NFL Countdown crew, which consists of host Mike Greenberg, Alex Smith, Teddy Bruschi, Randy Moss and Adam Schefter. As of now, according to a statement from an ESPN spokesperson, Ryan will be on the show, and there is no expectation that he’ll address the matter. “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.” Ryan also usually appears on the morning show “Get Up” on Mondays following the NFL slate, so it’s likely he’ll be on air for each of the next two days. From an ESPN spokesperson on Rex Ryan: “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.” Would not expect Ryan to address the matter on air. — Richard Deitsch (@richarddeitsch) November 15, 2026 Ryan’s Time as Jets Head Coach While Ryan coached the Bills for two years, he was best known for his six seasons as the Jets’ head coach. The last time New York won a playoff game was in 2011, when Ryan was still coaching the team. He compiled a 46-50 regular-season record but went 4-2 in the postseason, including back-to-back trips to the AFC Championship Game. Those appearances came during his first two seasons with the organization, while the four years that followed didn’t go as planned.
